newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks dip at open in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks dip at open in quiet trade.

text.p: CHANGE

* Toronto stocks dipped at the open on Friday as the gold sector continued to slide. * Trade was a thin 4.7 million shares worth C$64.5 million as U.S. markets were closed.
Toronto stocks dipped at the open on Friday in thin trade as the heavily weighted gold sector continued to slide on the back of weak bullion prices.
The precious metals sub-index was the only real mover as U.S. market players took a break for Independence Day.
"Golds continue to be weak. People just don't want them in their portfolios...they would be down more except that there's just no bids," one trader said.
But he said major institutional players were holding their golds in the absence of buyers: "I just think that it's too late in the game to be a major seller of them."

The sector was hit on Thursday as the price of gold dropped more than US$7 per ounce, and all the portents pointed to even lower gold prices next week after the metal fixed at an 11-1/2-year low of US$325.25 in London on Friday morning.
In early trade today, the gold sector was down 145.22 points or 1.79 percent at 7981.31.

Overall trade was narrower, with the Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipping 9.72 points to 6578.32 in light turnover of 4.7 million shares worth C$64.5 million. Declines outpaced advances 208 to 155, while 202 issues held steady.
"There's nothing going on. The tape is moving extremely slowly," the trader said.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes were down, led by golds. Utilities led the gainers.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Major golds hit by the sell-off included Placer Dome Inc, whose shares fell 0.80 to 20.90 in moderate trade, and Barrick Gold Corp, which fell 0.60 to 28.70.
